hints: Focus on what makes a structural isomer, same molecular formula but different connectivity of the carbon skeleton.
Count the carbons in Q first, every line end and every junction is a carbon, you should get 14 carbons in total for an alkane.
Check each option for total carbons and then for connectivity, identical structures drawn differently are not isomers.
walkthrough:
**Find the formula of Q**

Remember in skeletal formulae each end of a line is a $\text{CH}_3$ and each bend or branch point is a $\text{CH}_2$, $\text{CH}$ or $\text{C}$.

Counting all ends plus junctions in Q gives 14 carbons, so Q is $\text{C}_{14}\text{H}_{30}$.

**Count carbons in the options**

Do the same careful count for A, C and D, they all have 14 carbons.

Count B carefully and you get only 13 carbons, so B is $\text{C}_{13}\text{H}_{28}$ and cannot be an isomer.

**Identical or isomeric?**

A structural isomer must have the same formula but a different order of connections.

$$ \text{structural isomer: same } \text{C}_{14}\text{H}_{30} \text{, different branching} $$
A and D have the same long chain with methyl branches in the same places as Q, they are just drawn rotated. They are the same molecule as Q.

**Pick the true isomer**

C also has 14 carbons, so it has the same molecular formula $\text{C}_{14}\text{H}_{30}$.

But its branching is quite different, with adjacent branched carbons and an isopropyl branch in the middle, so the connectivity is different from Q. That is the structural isomer.

options.A: Has 14 carbons like Q but the connectivity is the same as Q. It is 2,3,5,7,8-pentamethylnonane drawn with the right hand end rotated, so it is the same molecule, not a structural isomer.
options.B: Has only 13 carbons in the skeleton, so its formula is $\text{C}_{13}\text{H}_{28}$ compared to $\text{C}_{14}\text{H}_{30}$ for Q. Different molecular formula means it cannot be a structural isomer.
options.C: Has 14 carbons like Q, so it shares the molecular formula $\text{C}_{14}\text{H}_{30}$, but the carbon skeleton is branched in a different way. Same formula with different connectivity is exactly a structural isomer.
options.D: Has 14 carbons like Q but the chain and methyl positions match Q exactly. It is the same molecule as Q drawn slightly differently, so it is not an isomer.
